sections.text: Four Rooms explodes through interconnected stories in LA's Hotel Mon Signor, following Ted the bellhop (Tim Roth) on his first night. Quentin Tarantino, Robert Rodriguez, Alexandre Rockwell, and Allison Anders each direct a segment, creating a wild anthology. The stories range from a witch coven's ritual gone wrong to a bet involving chopped fingers. Like Pulp Fiction meets Plaza Suite, each room reveals increasingly bizarre scenarios as Ted stumbles between them, desperately trying to maintain his professional composure while chaos erupts around him.

Tim Roth channels silent film legends like Buster Keaton and Charlie Chaplin, transforming Ted into a twitchy, over-eager bellhop whose physical performance carries the film. His exaggerated movements and facial expressions grow more frantic with each segment. The star-studded cast includes Madonna, Antonio Banderas, and Quentin Tarantino himself, though some performances veer into overacting - particularly in the witch coven segment. Roth's consistent character thread holds the disparate pieces together like Steve Buscemi did in Mystery Train.

Each segment's distinct visual approach mirrors its director's signature style. Rodriguez brings his kinetic energy to 'The Misbehavers,' while Tarantino's 'The Man from Hollywood' features his trademark long takes and pop culture dialogue. The transitions between styles can be jarring, but cinematographer Guillermo Navarro maintains visual cohesion through rich colors and dramatic lighting. The production design of the Hotel Mon Signor itself becomes a character, reminiscent of The Grand Budapest Hotel's meticulous world-building.

Four Rooms emerged during the 1990s independent film boom alongside Clerks and Reservoir Dogs, showcasing the era's experimental spirit. While not reaching those films' acclaim, it developed a cult following for its ambitious structure and genre-bending approach. The film influenced later anthology works like Sin City and Paris, je t'aime. Its biggest impact came from proving multiple auteur directors could collaborate on a single project, though the uneven final product showed the format's challenges.
